title: fix(sessions): reuse prepared sharing facts during publication
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-entry worker publication rebuilds a sharing projection that its owner already prepared, making the existing cancellation-ordering regression fail with four entry-shaped clones against its unchanged budget of three.

## User Impact

Removes a redundant publication clone without changing session contents, mutable patch results, commit ordering, or authority checks. No schema, configuration, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareSessionEntryReplacementChanges` computes the sharing projection once. Its current-publication reader omitted that fact, so `readPreparedSessionEntryChange` recomputed and cloned it when the replica subscriber read the publication. Carry the existing sharing projection through the same supersession check as the entry.

The regression starts at **36190da70d0e8797be4db0eec82b30479210393a**, PR #183276: its resident-entry lookup installs the replica subscription. The new subscriber exposed the missing prepared fact; the mutable-result copy in that PR is not the redundant clone. That copy remains intact.

Production LOC delta: **+1 / −0**. This adds the missing field to the existing owner result and eliminates repeated work; it adds no state, cache, or alternate path. The existing regression is unchanged, including its `<= 3` budget and nested caller-mutation assertion.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: the existing test must pass without changing its clone budget, committed facts must precede cancellation observers, and mutable caller results must remain isolated. This is deterministic owner work-count evidence, not a whole-Gateway latency or allocation claim.

| Revision | Focused regression samples | Entry-shaped `structuredClone` calls | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `ab17eb7b0c71` (`36190da7^`) | 1 | ≤3 | Pass |
| `36190da70d0e` (#183276) | 1 | 4 | Fail: `4 <= 3` |
| Current-main baseline `db38cc106695` | 2 | 4 | Fail: `4 <= 3` |
| Baseline + this fix | 1 | ≤3 | Pass, unchanged assertion |

The adjacent suspect and parent have identical lockfiles. Stack tracing on current main attributes the extra clone to `readPreparedSessionEntryChange` called by the replica subscriber. Temporary tracing was removed before validation.

Mac validation uses Node 26.12.1 to launch the repository test runner (which selects the pinned Bun test runtime and native workers). No Team workload or production state was touched.

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files below> --maxWorkers=1`: **50 tests passed in five files**, 56.53 s Vitest / 59.89 s wrapper wall time:

- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-session-row.test.ts`
- `src/config/sessions/session-entry-patch.operations.test.ts`
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-identity-publication.test.ts`
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-replacement-publication.test.ts`
- `src/config/sessions/session-actor-replica.test.ts`

Changed-file oxfmt, changed-file oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass. [CI run 40196731187](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40196731187) completed successfully on exact head `9d3cb2059aaa9ceecd5e7300adf4fabe5aae905a`, including all three changed-node test jobs, build artifacts, core lint, and all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs. The security-review workflow also passed. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no actionable P0–P2 findings, including supersession, unavailable-participant handling, and mutation isolation. Hosted Codex and ClawSweeper reviews also report no findings on this head.

After deployment, look for fewer `projectSessionSharingEntry` / `structuredClone` allocations from the replica publication reader during session metadata writes; this change does not predict a measurable whole-process GC or CPU shift. Linux and broad checks are covered by the linked CI run; no shipped-Gateway or production profiling claim is made. This PR is left open for maintainer verification and merge.
